html:
SCORM (Shareable Content Object Reference Model) is a set of technical standards used to create and deliver online training content. SCORM guides programmers on how to write their code so it can seamlessly integrate with other eLearning software. It is the de facto industry standard for eLearning interoperability, specifically governing the communication between online learning content and Learning Management Systems (LMSs). SCORM focuses solely on technical standards and does not address instructional design or any other content-related aspects.

Our SCORM packages are offered as part of an annual subscription and are licensed per seat (i.e., per user per year). While you can upload the SCORM file to your LMS, access is limited to the number of seats purchased. We do not offer a one-time purchase with unlimited access. You can preview a sample SCORM package on the course page, if the package doesn't work in your LMS, or you're not satisfied for any other reason, you're covered by our 30-day money-back guarantee. For a custom quote or further assistance, please contact our sales team via phone or email.

Once you select a course, use our interactive slider seat selector to choose the required seats. Adjust the quantity to see real-time pricing with discounts and complete your purchase instantly. After your order is received, you’ll receive a OneDrive link to download the SCORM package, which you can seamlessly integrate into your Learning Management System (LMS) for immediate access and tracking.

Using SCORM (Sharable Content Object Reference Model) offers several benefits for eLearning content creation and delivery: 

1. Interoperability: SCORM ensures that your eLearning content can work seamlessly across different Learning Management Systems (LMSs), making it easy to share and distribute. 

2. Reusability: SCORM-compliant content can be reused across multiple courses and platforms, saving time and resources in content creation. 

3. Consistency: By adhering to SCORM standards, you ensure a consistent learning experience for users, regardless of the LMS they use. 

4. Tracking and Reporting: SCORM enables detailed tracking of learner progress and performance, providing valuable data for assessments and improvements. 

5. Cost-Effectiveness: SCORM's interoperability and reusability reduce the need for custom development, lowering overall costs for eLearning projects. 

6. Industry Standard: As the de facto industry standard for eLearning interoperability, using SCORM ensures your content meets widely accepted technical requirements. 

By using SCORM, you enhance the flexibility, scalability, and efficiency of your eLearning programs, providing a better experience for both learners and administrators. 

Below is a brief overview of the main SCORM versions: 

1. SCORM 1.1 

  • The earliest version, introduced to standardize how learning content communicates with an LMS. 
  • Had limited adoption due to initial technical complexities. 

2. SCORM 1.2 

  • The most widely implemented version for many years and still in extensive use. 
  • Streamlined various issues found in SCORM 1.1 and provided more reliable data tracking. 

3. SCORM 2004 

  • Introduced advanced capabilities like sequencing and navigation controls. 
  • Released in multiple “editions” (1st through 4th) which refined and clarified specifications. 
  • The 4th edition is the most current iteration under the SCORM 2004 umbrella. 

Although SCORM 1.2 remains common in legacy systems, SCORM 2004 (particularly 4th Edition) is considered more robust, with its enhanced tracking and content navigation features. Depending on your LMS and organizational needs, you may choose one version over the other. If you are looking for newer approaches to tracking learner experiences, you might also explore newer standards like xAPI (Tin Can) or cmi5, though these fall outside the strict SCORM family. 

Each version builds upon the previous one and introduces new features and improvements. For example, SCORM 1.2 added support for multimedia content, while SCORM 2004 added support for more advanced tracking and reporting capabilities. 

The standard SCORM package is generated according to the SCORM 1.2 /SCORM 2004 (4th edition) standards, depending on the option you select, and will be shared with you within 24 hours after you complete your order. 

Custom branded SCORM package takes up to 7 business days after you place the order. 

We generally send a link from which you must download the SCORM package for your use. 

Integrating SCORM with your Learning Management System (LMS) is quite easy, provided you have the necessary access permissions to the LMS! Please follow the following steps: 

1. Upload SCORM Package to LMS: Log in to your LMS and locate the option to add or upload a new course/module. Select the SCORM package (ZIP file) and upload it to the LMS. 

2. Configure Course Settings: Configure the course settings in your LMS, such as course name, description, enrollment options, and tracking preferences. Ensure the SCORM-specific settings are correct, such as completion criteria, scoring, and reporting options. 

3. Test the Integration: Test the uploaded SCORM package to ensure it functions correctly within the LMS. Verify that the content loads properly, interactions work as intended, and tracking/reporting features are operational. 

4. Deploy to Learners: Once you’ve confirmed that everything is working correctly, assign the course to your learners. Provide necessary instructions or support to help them access and navigate the SCORM content. 

5. Monitor and Report: Use the LMS’s reporting and analytics features to monitor learner progress and performance. SCORM-compliant courses will provide detailed tracking data, such as completion status, quiz/exam scores, and time spent on each module. 

Most modern LMS platforms support SCORM 1.2 or SCORM 2004. However, it is always best to confirm compatibility with your LMS provider or test our demo module before purchasing.

SCORM plays a pivotal role in corporate compliance training by ensuring consistent, trackable content delivery across an organization. By standardizing how courses communicate with an LMS, SCORM enables employers to: 

1. Accurately Track Completion and Performance 

  • SCORM captures whether each employee has started, partially completed, or finished a course. It can also record quiz scores, time spent in modules, and other performance metrics. 
  • This data is crucial for demonstrating to regulators or auditors that mandated training has been successfully delivered and completed. 

2. Simplify Reporting and Record-Keeping 

  • Because SCORM content automatically reports completion status back to the LMS, administrators have a clear record of compliance across all required training programs. 
  • In the event of an audit or legal inquiry, these records can be easily retrieved to confirm that employees met the necessary training requirements on schedule. 

3. Support Organizational Consistency 

  • With SCORM-compliant courses, each employee—regardless of location or device—receives the same standardized content and assessment. 
  • Consistent training delivery helps eliminate gaps that could otherwise lead to compliance issues. 

4. Enable Ongoing Monitoring and Updates 

  • If regulations change, SCORM-based courses can be swiftly updated in one place, ensuring that new requirements are rolled out to all employees simultaneously. 
  • Real-time tracking and reporting allow compliance officers to see who has taken updated courses and whether additional follow-up is needed. 

SCORM packages are hosted within an LMS, which typically provides access controls, data encryption, and secure login mechanisms to protect content and learner data.

SCORM compliance is crucial for LMS platforms because it ensures seamless functionality and compatibility across different systems. With SCORM-compliant content, organizations can switch LMS providers without losing access to their learning materials, as these modules are designed to work universally. This flexibility also allows content to be reused across various departments, saving time and resources. 

Additionally, SCORM compliance guarantees a consistent and standardized learning experience for users, regardless of the platform. Furthermore, SCORM-compliant LMSs track learners’ progress and performance, providing valuable insights into course completion rates and learner engagement, which are essential for optimizing training strategies.

html:
Not sure if you or your team can complete the course? We've got you covered.

You get a full money-back guarantee within 30 days of purchase. After 30 days, we'll issue a credit for the full amount paid toward your next purchase, valid for 12 months.

To request a refund or credit, email info@oshascorm.org or call 1-866-429-6742 with your order number. We'll confirm receipt within 2 business days and process approved requests within 3-5 business days, to the original payment method where possible.

Renewals

Course licenses do not renew automatically. Before your license expires, we'll email you a renewal notice. Nothing is charged until you place a new order.

Our Guarantee

Guaranteed delivery. Standard SCORM packages are delivered within 24 hours of successful payment. Custom-branded (white-label) packages are delivered within 7 business days.

Guaranteed value. If you find the identical course package offered elsewhere at a lower price within 30 days of purchase, send us the listing and we'll refund the difference.

Guaranteed satisfaction. If you're not satisfied, notify us in writing and we'll work with you to make it right, subject to the terms in the Return Policy above.

Technical support. Free technical support for installation and performance issues is included for 12 months from purchase. Call 1-866-429-6742, Monday–Friday, 7:00 AM–5:00 PM CST, or email info@oshascorm.org.
